newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down but still in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down but still in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended lower across the board Tuesday in a moderate session, but prices remained in recent ranges amid little reason to move far in either direction, sources said.
May slipped three cents to close at $1.916 per million British thermal units. June settled 3.2 cents lower at $1.977. Other deferreds ended down 1.8 to six cents.

"Right now, we're just range trading. It's not rallying and it's not failing, but I don't think the market can do much fundamentally near-term," said one New York futures trader, adding significant weakness should prompt end-user buying.

Traders said 11-15 day forecasts today calling for more below to much-below normal Midwest and Northeast weather could continue to support the market, particularly with spreads still favoring early injections.
But few expect much upside, with inventories well ahead of last year and likely to remain that way for quite some time.
Technical traders agreed the market was range-bound, with good resistance in May at $2, then at $2.045-2.05 and $2.10. Support was still pegged at $1.825-1.85.
Early estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA gas stock report ranged from a draw of 10 bcf to a build of 30 bcf. For the same week last year, stocks fell by 15 bcf.

Colder Midwest and eastern weather forecasts firmed physical prices slightly Tuesday. Gulf Coast prices climbed a couple of cents to the $1.95-2.00 area. Midcontinent pipes were up a similar amount to $1.85-1.90. Gas at New York city gate again jumped more than 10 cents to the mid-to-high $2.30s on the approaching cold.
NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip fell 2.5 cents to $2.114. NYMEX said 29,852 Hub contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 26,764.
No Permian or Alberta natgas futures traded Tuesday.
On KCBT, May finished 3.5 cents lower at $1.76, while deferreds ended down by one to two cents. The East/West spread widened by one-half cent to 15.6 cents (NYMEX premium).
